audit.whatIsWrong: The two layers disagree on four of seven rows (full: Zed/Skill/Skill/Skill/Zed/Skill/Skill; content and packet: Orianna/Skill/Skill/Zed/Skill/Zed/Orianna). Worse, content whys[3] sits on the Levels 4-5 row and reads 'with R up Zed's all-in burst (R + shadow Q + ignite)' — Zed has no ultimate at 4-5.
audit.why: packet.levelChart matches content win[], so the full layer moves. The why on row 3 describes level 6 and had to be rewritten to something true at 4-5: his abilities cost energy that his shadows refund, your Q costs 35 mana, and his Q reaches 900 to your 815.
audit.corrected: phases[0].side -> Orianna, phases[3].side -> Zed, phases[4].side -> Skill, phases[5].side -> Zed, phases[6].side -> Orianna, each moved row's why rewritten. whys[2] and whys[3] realigned to Level 3 and Levels 4-5.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level 6 row claimed 'your lane presence doubles', and dosFull[2].d called Death Mark a 'fifteen-second invitation'.
audit.why: Death Mark is 120/110/100s and the mark triggers 3 seconds after it lands; Command: Shockwave is 110/95/80s. Fifteen seconds is not any number in either kit.
audit.corrected: Row 4 now states the 120s vs 110s ult trade and why the read is even; dosFull[2].d states the real 120-second cooldown as the reason to own a Stopwatch before he hits 6.

audit.whatIsWrong: packet.defects: the full layer never names a Zed ability beyond Death Mark, and breakdown.cooldowns held no numbers or mechanics.
audit.why: Kit: Death Mark 120/110/100s, untargetable dash, mark repeats a portion of damage after 3 seconds. Living Shadow 20/19/18/17/16s — the shadow stays and he can swap to it, so it is escape and engage. Shadow Slash 5s down to 3s, 290 radius, slows only from a shadow's slash. Razor Shuriken 900. Orianna's answers are E at 9s and R at 110s.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns rebuilt on Death Mark's 120s and 3-second trigger and Living Shadow's 20s; dosFull[0].d now explains the untargetable dash and the 3-second window your 9s shield has to cover; dosFull[1].d explains the shadow swap as the real Shockwave target.

audit.whatIsWrong: Copy-paste bleed in dosFull[1].d and dontsFull[2].d (both carried the tradeGood/tradeBad strings), and the content whys refer to Orianna as 'she/her' rather than addressing the reader.
audit.why: Defect-catalogue item 2 plus the second-person voice the bar requires.
audit.corrected: Bodies rewritten to their own titles; whys moved into second person.

edits.before: Luden's spike: Q-W chunks a third of his bar. Shove, rotate, and let the ball-delivery threat run the river fights.
edits.after: His Youmuu's beats your Luden's here: he roams, picks and dives, and one bad ball placement is a Death Mark.

edits.before: Late Ori is the teamfight: protect-ball on your diver, shockwave their clump, and dissonance the choke they retreat through.
edits.after: Grouped you win: Death Mark takes one target while Shockwave takes their clump — keep the ball on whoever he marks.

edits.before: Zed wins by landing Death Mark, denying your pattern, and starting the fight your kit wanted ten seconds later.
edits.after: Zed wins by baiting your stopwatch, marking you with Death Mark, and repeating a share of it three seconds later.

edits.before: - Zed Death Mark: matchup-defining — The all-in — spend your defensive answer AFTER the mark lands, not before. Check it before every step-up. - E Command: Protect is the lifeline; chip damage never gets it. - The ult answers fights, not waves.
edits.after: - Death Mark: 120s at rank 1 — the mark triggers after 3 seconds, so your Stopwatch goes in AFTER it lands, never before. - Living Shadow: 20s at rank 1, 16s at rank 5 — that is his escape as well as his engage. - Your E is 9s: keep it for the mark.

edits.before: Carry through the ball — no champion controls teamfight space like Orianna; one Shockwave on three is a won game, and you decide when it happens.
edits.after: Carry through the ball — Zed can only take one target, so hold the ball on whoever he marks and the Shockwave that follows ends him instead.

edits.before: The all-in — spend your defensive answer AFTER the mark lands, not before. Commit on its cooldown, never into it.
edits.after: He is untargetable during the dash, so the ball comes home first — the 9s shield is up before the 3s mark expires.

edits.before: Ball on his farm path, Q-W the last-hit contact, auto-weave once, and recall the ball — three-second trades his combo math can't answer.
edits.after: Living Shadow swaps him to where the shadow stands — drop the ball on that spot and R the swap, not the body you are looking at.

edits.before: Zed burns Death Mark on nothing — take the fifteen-second invitation.
edits.after: Stopwatch beats a 120-second ultimate: buy it before he reaches 6.

edits.before: That’s Zed’s bread-and-butter play — deny it and they run out of answers.
edits.after: With the ball 815 away when Death Mark lands you have no shield at all.

edits.before: Poking with the ball stranded at max range when his engage is up — an Orianna without her ball is a Doran's Ring with legs.
edits.after: Your Q costs 35 mana and his shadows refund energy — the third greedy poke is the one he answers with Death Mark.

edits.before: Orianna — pre-6 she out-ranges Zed and wins the early trades with ball poke, dominating the level 1-3 phase.
edits.after: Orianna — pre-6 you out-range Zed and win the early trades with ball poke, owning the level 1-3 phase.

edits.before: Skill — the early-to-mid transition trades hinge on execution: her poke vs his shadow-Q spacing.
edits.after: Skill — at 2 the trade hinges on execution: your Q-W poke against his 900-range shadow-Q spacing.

edits.before: Skill — around the level 6 tipping point it's about who uses cooldowns better before ults define the fight.
edits.after: Skill — at 3 his Shadow Slash is a 5s slow and your E shield lands; whoever misuses a cooldown loses the trade.

edits.before: Zed — with R up Zed's all-in burst (R + shadow Q + ignite) beats Orianna unless she perfectly times stasis.
edits.after: Zed — his energy costs nothing while your Q burns 35 a cast, so he out-pokes you at 900 through 4-5.

edits.before: Zed — as a roaming assassin Zed wins the isolated pick and side-lane skirmish where Orianna is exposed.
edits.after: Zed — with Youmuu's he roams and wins the isolated pick and side-lane skirmish where you are exposed.

edits.before: Orianna — in grouped 5v5 teamfights her Shockwave and utility outclass Zed, who can only pick stragglers.
edits.after: Orianna — grouped, your Shockwave and shields outclass a Zed who is left only picking off stragglers.

notes: The Levels 4-5 row was the worst defect here: the page told a reader Zed wins that stage because of his R + shadow Q + ignite all-in, and Zed does not have an ultimate at levels 4-5. The replacement is grounded in the kit — his abilities cost energy his shadows refund, your Q costs 35 mana, and his Q reaches 900 to your 815. wants.foe[4] ('Serpent's Fang / Edge of Night to beat your shield and CC') is item behaviour not present in the kit data and was left unedited. spikes[] entries are Zed-specific and accurate but written in the third person about Orianna; left as-is rather than lose content squeezing them into the length band. phases[N].rating untouched.
